# Measure Findings: Calendar Event Popup
**AI-generated by:** Alson (A.I Agent)

## Result

The calendar popup implementation has a conditional local pass. Automated coverage and static checks pass, and the existing server-side participant authorization tests remain green. Authenticated browser and responsive visual evidence are still required.

## Acceptance Results

| Criterion | Result | Evidence or gap |
|---|---|---|
| Desktop event selection opens popup | Implemented locally | `calendar-view.tsx` binds event markers to the selected-event dialog; authenticated browser review remains open |
| Mobile event selection opens popup | Implemented locally | `calendar-view.tsx` binds mobile event rows to the same dialog; authenticated browser review remains open |
| Event details are shown | Pass locally | Existing title, date/time, description, optional location, and live broadcast link are rendered in the dialog |
| Administrator Edit and Delete actions | Pass locally | Actions are rendered only when `isAdmin` is true; existing edit and delete callbacks are preserved |
| Participant actions are absent | Pass locally by implementation and role payload | Calendar feature tests assert `is_admin=false` for participants; authenticated browser review remains open |
| Participant direct mutations are denied | Pass locally | `CalendarTest` covers forbidden participant edit and delete requests |
| Dialog close and edit transition | Implemented locally | Controlled dialog state clears before the existing edit form opens; browser interaction evidence remains open |
| Responsive behavior | Conditional | Desktop and mobile render paths are implemented; visual review is not recorded |
| Protected calendar route | Pass locally | Guest request to `/calendar` redirects to `/login` |

## Decision Boundary

Measure result: **conditional local pass**. The implementation may continue to authenticated browser review. This run does not authorize staging, production, or final launch acceptance.
